answer.answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally attaches “upon SFC’s request” to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned by a request. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; demonstration expressly must satisfy the SFC. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content for both confirmation and demonstration, but its unqualified wording leaves a rival reading that demonstration is also a standing requirement. On the harmonised reading, no request means demonstration is not yet triggered, while confirmation and underlying requirements remain. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining an audit or verification, and a satisfactory legal opinion, on the relevant SFC request. None of these trigger conclusions establishes fulfillment.

claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 supports standing confirmation and request-triggered demonstration concerning the same three subjects, with an express SFC-satisfaction standard for demonstration.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request condition immediately precedes “demonstrate”; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” most directly qualifies demonstration. The listed subjects apply to both verbs. This does not establish that confirmation requires no substantive evidential basis.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the Product Provider, product, activity and assessment period.
Any applicable conditions or further guidance specifying confirmation procedure or evidential requirements.

claims.proposition: Footnote 5 adds minimum confirmation and demonstration content: compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and high confidence concerning absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

claims.inference: Text: footnote 5 expressly addresses both confirmation and demonstration and supplies minimum content. Its high-confidence wording most directly concerns absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws. Judgment: reading it as elaborating paragraph 14 preserves both that content and the main-text request condition; reading its unqualified demonstration language independently supports a competing standing-duty interpretation.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of how the footnote and main-text request condition interact.
An applicable evidential meaning of “high level of confidence” and the SFC’s satisfaction standard.

claims.proposition: No SFC request does not remove confirmation or underlying substantive requirements, and its effect on demonstration depends on the retained reading.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

claims.inference: Conditional deduction: assuming applicability and actual absence of a relevant request, readings A and C leave demonstration untriggered; reading B still requires it. Confirmation remains under each reading. An untriggered demonstration requirement neither proves soundness nor discharges underlying responsibilities. Absence of evidence of a request is not itself proof that none was made.
missing_premises: Actual request history and the scope and timing of any request.
Facts showing confirmation and substantive compliance.
Resolution of the rival demonstration readings.

claims.proposition: Paragraphs 15 and 16 impose distinct request-triggered requirements to obtain external assurance or legal support; neither is identical to paragraph 14 confirmation or demonstration.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: each paragraph expressly conditions obtaining its specified item on an SFC request. Paragraph 15 concerns third-party audit or verification of the same three subjects; paragraph 16 concerns a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. A paragraph 14 demonstration request does not automatically establish a request for either item, though one actual request could cover multiple requirements. Paragraph 15 does not expressly repeat the SFC-satisfaction or high-confidence wording; paragraph 16 expressly requires a satisfactory opinion.
missing_premises: Content and scope of any SFC request under each provision.
Applicable standards for the audit or verification and for a satisfactory legal opinion.
Evidence that the requested item was obtained and met the applicable standard.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: confirmation is standing; demonstration of paragraph 14’s three subjects is request-triggered and must satisfy the SFC. This reading leaves the precise attachment of footnote 5’s content and standard unresolved; it cannot justify ignoring the footnote.

B — Independent-footnote reading: footnote 5’s unqualified “confirm and demonstrate” supports standing demonstration of its minimum content, even without a request. The express main-text request condition is countervailing evidence.

C — Harmonised reading: confirmation remains standing; demonstration is request-triggered and must satisfy the SFC; footnote 5 supplies minimum content for both. This best preserves the main-text trigger and footnote content together, but remains an interpretive judgment.
unresolved: The retained text does not conclusively resolve the competing trigger readings or fully specify confirmation procedure, evidential sufficiency, SFC satisfaction or high confidence.
Actual applicability, request history, confirmation, operational facts and supporting evidence are absent; neither compliance nor breach is established.
The provisions use “should”; their precise legal effect depends on the applicable regulatory context and conditions.
The supplied solver and round-trip results concern encoded representations and do not establish source-to-rule fidelity or legal truth.
